one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-08. Scheduled: TMUS Q3 2026 results and call on 2026-10-28 [39]; Verizon and AT&T Q3 reports also fall in late October (exact dates not confirmed by me). Management already pre-guided Q3 postpaid net account adds to ~250K (vs ~304K Street at the time) with temporarily elevated account churn from the legacy-plan migration [37], so a weak headline is largely known; upside risk is that the migration lifts ARPA and FY FCF guidance (already raised to $18.4-18.8B [1]) is reaffirmed or raised; downside risk is a 2027 commentary that concedes more promotional intensity (iPhone 18 'up to $1,200' trade-ins, cable free-line offers [34,28]). The stock just fell 13.3% in one session (2026-10-09) on SpaceX's 800 MHz purchase with VZ -8.8% and T -9.8% [30], a sector-wide shock on news whose service impact is years away (5G-class Starlink Mobile targeted 1H28 [33]); short-term reversal after such gaps argues for a slight upward lean, but further FCC/SpaceX headlines and rate moves (10y at 5.22% [41], Sept FOMC hike [34]) cut the other way. Net: near-neutral median ~$149 with monthly vol ~11% (a bit above 33%/3.5=9.4% because of the earnings event and post-shock volatility).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (60%): FY27 consensus EPS $14.44 haircut 5% to $13.72 x 12.0x = $164.6, and EV/EBITDA (40%): 2027E core EBITDA $38.8B x 7.5x less $117.6B net debt over 1,030M shares = $168.3; blended $166.

methods.inputs: FY2027 EPS $13.72 (consensus $14.44 less 5%) x 12.0x (peer median 9.9x, range 2.3-15.5x)

inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis/S&P Global consensus; cross-check Alpha Vantage FY27 average $13.94 (22 analysts).

$14.44 x 0.95 = $13.72. 5% haircut for incremental competitive pressure (cable record line adds, Charter $1,000 switching guarantee, SpaceX entering with 800 MHz + 2 GHz); lands just below the lower Alpha Vantage consensus $13.94.

Peer median fwd P/E 9.9x (range 2.3x-15.5x across 10 peers). 12.0x is inside the range, ~21% above median, vs TMUS EPS growth 16.5% that is ~1.9x the peer median growth of 8.9%; PEG 0.73 vs peer ~1.1. TMUS trades 11.8x today.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2027E EBITDA $38.8B x 7.5x = $291.0B EV; net debt $117.6B; 1,030M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: $37.3B x 1.04 = $38.8B; 4% growth matches consensus FY27 revenue growth of +4.4% (StockAnalysis), well below Q2-26 core EBITDA growth of +11.7% which was boosted by acquisitions.
Peer median EV/EBITDA 6.9x (trailing; range 4.6x-9.7x). TMUS trades 8.06x trailing today. 7.5x on forward EBITDA is inside the range and below current, giving a smaller premium than on P/E.
StockAnalysis net debt $117.6B. Held flat because 2026 adj FCF guidance $18.4-18.8B roughly equals the $18.2B shareholder-return authorization, so FCF is returned rather than used to delever.
1,074.8M at 2026-06-30 minus ~45M = Q2-26 pace of 11.4M shares/quarter x 4 quarters.

bear.story: Industry repricing: cable keeps taking ~850K+ lines/quarter between Comcast and Charter with free-line and $1,000 switching offers [28,27,29], Verizon and AT&T keep posting 184K-432K phone adds [25,26], SpaceX wins FCC approval and bids in the April-2027 upper C-band auction [32], and investors capitalize a share-loss narrative. TMUS FY27 EPS slips to ~$13 and the multiple compresses to the peer median (~9x incl. rates at 5%+) = ~$112-117.

base.story: Legacy-plan migration lifts ARPA after a Q3 churn blip [37]; FY26 guidance met; FY27 EPS ~$13.7-14.4; Starlink Mobile remains a 2028 story with coverage-not-capacity spectrum (79 MHz vs 280-380 MHz per carrier [33]) and a $50-130B build bill [32], so the overhang caps rather than collapses the multiple at ~11.5-12x. Price ~$160, below the $166 fair value because the overhang persists through the horizon.

bull.story: Deutsche Telekom proceeds with the holding-company stock offer it was exploring in April 2026 [42,40], and/or satellite fears fade as Verizon/AT&T and TMUS show stable churn while subsidies decline industry-wide [25,38]; multiple re-rates to ~15x FY27 EPS $14.44 = ~$215.

comps_summary.peer_range: Fwd P/E 2.3x (CHTR) to 15.5x (TU); EV/EBITDA 4.6x (CMCSA) to 9.7x (TU). EV/EBITDA figures are StockAnalysis trailing (TTM) values; forward EV/EBITDA was not available from accessible free sources, so the ev_ebitda_fwd field holds the trailing figure for every peer. Peer next-year EPS growth median 8.9% (range 0.9%-20.3%). CHT (Chunghwa) was considered but dropped for missing forecast data; Telefonica page unavailable.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: P/E 12.0x vs peer median 9.9x (inside range; about the 70th percentile, between AMX 10.9x and VOD 13.6x). EV/EBITDA 7.5x forward vs 6.9x trailing median (inside range). TMUS itself trades 11.8x fwd P/E and 8.06x trailing EV/EBITDA.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A ~20% P/E premium is supported by structurally faster growth that is visible in reported numbers rather than sell-side calls: TMUS Q2-26 service revenue +8.9% and postpaid service revenue +12.6% with core EBITDA +11.7% [1], versus Verizon guiding mobility+broadband service revenue +2.5-3% for 2026 [25] and AT&T wireless service revenue +3.3% [26]; consensus FY27 EPS growth 16.5% vs peer median 8.9% [3]. On PEG the premium is still a discount (0.73 vs ~1.1). The premium is kept modest (not the 20x+ TMUS historically carried) because the advantage is under attack within the horizon: cable's record line adds [27,28], Verizon/AT&T phone-add recovery [25,26], and SpaceX's spectrum build-out [30-33]. Peer multiples themselves were depressed on 2026-10-09 by the same SpaceX shock and 5%+ yields [41].

thesis_break_reason: $115 is ~8.4x FY27 consensus EPS ($14.44) and roughly the peer median multiple applied to a haircut EPS; a TMUS trading there would mean the market is pricing an actual earnings downgrade (industry price cut / ARPA decline, or loss of postpaid account growth in Q3-Q4 reports), not just the Starlink sentiment overhang and rates. Below it, the faster-growth premium that underpins the base case is gone.

key_uncertainties: Whether Starlink Mobile becomes a price-led national competitor before 2028 or stays a coverage/rural niche (79 MHz vs 280-380 MHz per incumbent; $50-130B terrestrial build).
How much of TMUS's legacy-plan migration turns into churn versus ARPA gains; TMUS no longer reports postpaid phone net adds, which reduces visibility.
Cable share gains (Comcast free-year promo, Charter $1,000 switching guarantee) and whether Verizon's subsidy-light recovery holds.
Rates: 10-year at 5.22% after a September hike pressures leveraged telecom multiples sector-wide.
Deutsche Telekom combination: structure, premium, political approvals all unknown.
Divergence in consensus EPS between data providers (FY27 $14.44 vs $13.94) reflects adjusted vs reported definitions.
reasoning: Lane: industry. Facts from TMUS's own Q2 filing (service revenue +8.9%, core EBITDA +11.7%, FCF guidance raised to $18.4-18.8B, 1,074.8M shares) set the base [1]. The chain says: (a) incumbents have recovered - Verizon posted 184K phone adds and guided upper half of 750K-1M while cutting subsidies [25], AT&T posted 432K with churn 0.86% [26]; (b) cable is the steady share taker - Comcast record 448K lines on a free-year promo, Charter 406K [28,27], Recon flags Charter's $1,000 switching guarantee and TMUS's reporting going dark below accounts [29]; (c) TMUS itself pre-guided a weak Q3 (~250K accounts vs ~304K est.) from forced legacy-plan migration [37]; (d) the 2026-10-09 -13.3% day was a sector shock on SpaceX buying Grain's 800 MHz (ex-TMUS) spectrum, with VZ -8.8% and T -9.8% [30,31]; trade and sell-side analysis says this is coverage not capacity (79 MHz vs 280-380 MHz), build cost $50-130B, 5G-class service 1H28 [32,33]. So the threat is real but mostly beyond the 12-month horizon, while rates (10y 5.22%) and a Sept FOMC hike weigh on the group [41,34]. Valuation: P/E 12x on haircut FY27 EPS $13.72 = $165 and EV/EBITDA 7.5x on 2027E $38.8B = $168, blended $166; peer set of 10 telcos/cablecos has median 9.9x fwd P/E, 6.9x EV/EBITDA. Scenarios $112/$160/$215 at 25/50/25% (mean ~$162). The ladder is a mixture of lognormals around those scenarios (sigma 0.16-0.21 each), with tails widened for a stock down 34% in a year: P(>=149)=0.60, median ~$161. I deliberately keep the base below fair value because the Starlink overhang and high yields should persist through Oct-2027, and 12-month price momentum is strongly negative. No prediction market on Starlink Mobile or a DT/TMUS merger was found (only an unrelated Kalshi Starlink-IPO contract), so none is used. Twelve Data statistics and estimates were paywalled; Alpha Vantage hit its daily limit after one call; T-Mobile newsroom, Charter IR, Fierce and PhoneArena returned 403, so those figures came from the 8-K summary and trade press instead.
